results.answer: Metro Phoenix had 27,427 active listings in October 2026 (+6.8% YoY), 6,347 under contract and 5,155 closed sales, in a buyer's market. No source on agents' year-end 2026 marketing budgets was found.

facts.claim: Active listings across Metro Phoenix rose 6.8% year over year to 27,427 in October 2026, while listings under contract fell 13.5% to 6,347 (AZ Big Media, 2026-11-18).
facts.quote: Active listings across Metro Phoenix increased 6.8% year over year to 27,427 in October, while listings under contract dropped 13.5% to 6,347
facts.sourceTitle: Metro Phoenix housing market shifts deeper into buyers' territory

facts.claim: Metro Phoenix closed sales totaled 5,155 in October 2026, down 9.8% from October 2025 (AZ Big Media, 2026-11-18).
facts.quote: Closed sales totaled 5,155, representing a 9.8% decline from a year earlier.
facts.sourceTitle: Metro Phoenix housing market shifts deeper into buyers' territory

results.notes: Article does not name ARMLS as data source. No survey of Arizona agents' year-end marketing budgets found; budget part unanswered.

results.answer: Published Phoenix-area drone prices: Fullview-360 (Mesa/Phoenix) drone packages $249 / $399 / $599; PropPhoto lists Mesa drone video as typically $129–$300 per shoot ($100–300 as an add-on). No Phoenix source states an average for the exact 10–15 photo + 1–2 min video package.

facts.claim: Fullview-360 (Mesa & Phoenix) sells an Essential drone package at $249 (standard drone photos, 2 angles, plus a 15–25 second drone video or 360 aerial pano), a Premium package at $399 and a Luxury package at $599 (8–10 drone shots, 30–50 second video).
facts.quote: Essential Package ($249) ... Standard Drone Photos 2 Angles ... 15-25 Second Drone Video or 360 Aerial Panoramic Photo

facts.claim: PropPhoto lists real estate drone video in Mesa, Arizona as typically $129 to $300 per shoot, with typical add-on pricing of $100–300 and standard delivery of 24–48 hours.
facts.sourceTitle: Book a real estate photographer today - Drone video in Mesa, AZ (PropPhoto)

failed: https://sites.google.com/view/joshsdroneservice/real-estate-services: opened, prices from $80 but no location stated, so not recorded as Phoenix
results.notes: Search snippets mentioned Snap2Close $89 drone video upgrade and Shefrin $100 aerial add-on in Phoenix but pages not opened/failed; not recorded.

results.answer: Industry practice sources say real estate photographers typically get paid at the shoot or before photos are delivered; some invoice net 30 monthly. No Phoenix-specific source found.

facts.claim: A real estate photography industry blog (Photography for Real Estate, 2016) advises that photos are not delivered before the invoice is paid.
facts.quote: you don't deliver the photos before the invoice is paid
facts.sourceTitle: When Should Real Estate Photographers Get Paid?

facts.claim: Real estate photographers commenting on that article report being paid in full at the shoot, while another invoices clients net 30 on the 1st of the month for the prior month's work (2016).
facts.quote: I get paid in full at the shoot.
facts.sourceTitle: When Should Real Estate Photographers Get Paid?

results.notes: Source is dated (2016) and national, reader comments are anecdotal. Fullview-360 and PropPhoto pages state no payment terms.

results.answer: No Phoenix MLS listing-level share was found. Nationally, NAR's 2025 Technology Survey says 52% of agents use drone photography/video, and HomeJab's 2025 order data shows aerial photos/video were added to 14.2% of shoots (13.0% in 2024).

facts.claim: NAR's 2025 technology survey (released 2025-09-18) found drone photography and video are used by 52% of US agents.
facts.quote: Drone photography and video are used by 52% of agents,
facts.sourceTitle: Realtors Embrace AI, Digital Tools to Enhance Client Service, NAR Survey Finds

facts.claim: In HomeJab's national 2025 order data, aerial (drone) photos/video were part of 14.2% of orders, up from 13.0% in 2024.
facts.sourceTitle: What HomeJab Customers Bought in 2025: An End-of-Year Look at Real Estate Media Trends

results.notes: No Phoenix/ARMLS data on the share of listings with drone media found.

results.answer: Arizona construction volume is projected at $31.1B in 2026 and $35.5B in 2027 (BEX). No source on Arizona firms' year-end budgets for drone surveying was found.

facts.claim: BEX projects Arizona construction volume of $31.1B in 2026 and $35.5B in 2027 (AZBEX, 2026-02-06).
facts.quote: In 2026, the data indicate Arizona Construction will see a volume of $31.1B
facts.sourceTitle: BEX Forecast Event Shows Construction Market Presented Exceptional Resilience, Flexibility in 2025

results.notes: Figures are projections. No evidence found on drone-surveying-specific procurement or year-end budgets.

results.answer: No Phoenix provider publishes drone mapping rates. A national 2026 guide gives $10–$30/acre for a basic orthomosaic, $50–$150/acre for engineering topo with ground control, and $500–$1,500 minimums for small sites (a 5-acre lot might be a flat $800).

facts.claim: SkyeBrowse's 2026 national survey cost guide puts a basic drone orthomosaic at roughly $10 to $30 per acre and an engineering topographic deliverable with ground control at $50 to $150 per acre.
facts.quote: roughly $10 to $30 per acre for a basic orthomosaic
facts.sourceTitle: Drone Survey Cost in 2026: Per-Acre Rates, Hire vs DIY, and Software

facts.claim: The same 2026 guide says small drone survey sites usually carry a $500 to $1,500 minimum, and a 5-acre lot might be a flat $800 project.
facts.quote: Small sites usually carry a $500 to $1,500 minimum.
facts.sourceTitle: Drone Survey Cost in 2026: Per-Acre Rates, Hire vs DIY, and Software

results.notes: Source is a software vendor's national guide, not Arizona-specific. Phoenix providers found (The Future 3D, Bugzeye, Elite Drone Services) quote on request only, per search results; their pages were not opened.

results.answer: Vendor sources put end-to-end turnaround at 4–8 hours for a standard construction site, with 30–90 minutes on site and 1–4 hours of cloud processing. Propeller's standard photogrammetry processing is 24 hours for uploads up to 20 gigapixels, and these are often delivered in under 12 hours.

facts.claim: A 2026 drone surveying guide estimates field capture through client hand-off at 4–8 hours for a standard construction or land development site, with on-site capture of 30–90 minutes and cloud upload/processing of 1–4 hours.
facts.quote: 4–8 hours for a standard construction or land development site
facts.sourceTitle: Drone Surveying: A Complete Guide to UAV Survey Methods, Accuracy, and Cost

facts.claim: Propeller Aero's data services description says photogrammetry surveys up to 20 gigapixels are often delivered in less than 12 hours (standard 24-hour timeframe).
facts.quote: Surveys up to 20 GP are often delivered in less than 12 hours.

results.notes: The guide's figures are vendor estimates and are not independently verified.

results.answer: On Arizona private construction, a law firm's summary says billings are deemed approved 14 days after receipt, the owner then pays within 7 days, and a contractor must pay subcontractors within 7 days of receiving payment. Actual contract terms used by firms for drone subcontractors were not found.

facts.claim: Under Arizona's Prompt Payment Act as summarized by Lang & Klain (2026), a contractor must pay subcontractors within seven days of receiving payment from the owner.
facts.quote: within seven days of its own receipt of payment from the owner.

facts.claim: Per the same Arizona Prompt Payment Act summary, the owner must issue the progress payment to the general contractor within seven days after the billing is deemed approved (14 days after receipt unless disputed).
facts.quote: The owner must issue the progress payment to the general contractor within seven days thereafter.

results.notes: Statute text could not be opened directly. Whether a drone data vendor counts as a 'subcontractor' under the Act, and whether parties may contract out of it, were not verified. The 7-day subcontractor clock starts only after the GC is paid, so total time from delivery can be about 4+ weeks.

results.answer: Phoenix aerial clips are licensed on Axiom Images ($69 for 4K H264, $199 for 4K ProRes per clip) and Getty Images. No source shows the volume of buyers searching for Arizona drone footage.

facts.claim: Axiom Images sells a 5.7K aerial stock clip of Downtown Phoenix, Arizona at $69 for a 4K UHD H264 download and $199 for a 4K ProRes HQ 10-bit download.
facts.quote: 5.7K aerial stock footage of flying by and away from the city's skyline, seen from homes in Downtown Phoenix, Arizona
facts.sourceTitle: Axiom Images - Aerial Stock Footage DX0002_140_012

results.notes: The price is the buyer price for the clip, not what the contributor earns. Axiom is the footage owner's library, not an open contributor marketplace. No platform publishes Arizona-specific buyer demand. Search results also showed Getty and Adobe Stock Phoenix aerial clips; those pages were not opened.

results.answer: Shutterstock pays contributors 15%–40% of license revenue for video, in six levels that reset to level 1 every January 1. Pond5 pays 30% non-exclusive and 40% exclusive on video (secondary source). Adobe Stock pays 35% on video per an Adobe Community Expert; Adobe's official page returned 403.

facts.claim: Shutterstock contributors earn under 6 earnings levels for images and for videos ranging from 15% to 40%, and levels reset to level 1 every January 1 (Shutterstock contributor help, updated 2025-04-21).
facts.quote: Levels for all contributors will reset to level 1 on January 1st of each year.
facts.sourceTitle: How much will I be paid as a contributor to Shutterstock?

facts.claim: Pond5 video royalties are 30% for non-exclusive contributors and 40% for Pond5 exclusives, with a $25 minimum payout threshold (StockPhotoSecrets, updated 2025-09-18).
facts.sourceTitle: What You Need to Know About Earning on Pond5: Percentages, Potential, Minimum Payouts

facts.claim: An Adobe Community Expert stated in January 2025 that Adobe Stock contributor royalty rates are 33% for images and 35% for videos. In the same thread, a contributor reported earning 2 USD on one video sale.
facts.quote: Royalty rates are 33% for images, 35% for videos.
facts.sourceTitle: Net income on videos - Adobe Community

results.notes: The Shutterstock page does not list the percentage for each level. The quoted lines record the reset rule and the Pond5 payout minimum; the 15–40%, 30%/40% and 35% figures come from the same opened pages, as reported by the fetch tool.
